To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MK-801 increases food intake, which is mediated by cholinergic neurons.
MK-801 increases sucrose consumption, an effect that is dependent on cholinergic mechanisms.
MK-801-induced feeding is mediated, at least in part, by an action on peripheral muscarinic receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of cholinergic neurotransmission in the feeding response and the role that cholinergic neurotransmitter plays in the regulation of gastric emptying.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the feeding response induced by NMDAR blockade.
the mechanisms by which the NMDA-glycine receptor complex regulates food intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cholinergic system is involved in the increased food intake induced via the blockade of the NMDA receptors.
the NMDA receptor antagonist, MK-801, induces feeding via an indirect action on peripheral cholinergic pathways.
MK-801-induced feeding is mediated, at least in part, through the vagus nerve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MK-801-induced feeding is dependent upon vagal cholinergic mechanisms.
MK-801, through an action in the hindbrain, increases food intake via a peripheral musca-rinic cholinergic pathway.
the NMDA receptor is involved in the control of food intake and the cholinergic system is a key player in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cholinergic system in the periphery plays a role in the increased feeding response to MK-801.
the NMDA receptor antagonist, MK-801, induces a cholinergically mediated increase in food intake.
the vagus is a major player in feeding induced by blockade of NMDARs.
